messages.text: Chickpea allergy here. Becoming a real problem now that everyone treats hummus as a default snack.

I bet. Chickpeas are everywhere in modern American restaurants — buddha bowls, hummus everything, falafel, chana masala in Indian. Most other legumes (lentils, black beans, white beans) usually don't cross-react.
Right. Need a creamy dip for a party that gives the hummus vibe without the chickpeas.

## Red Lentil Hummus

Similar texture, distinctive earthy flavor, no chickpeas anywhere.

**Method**
Cook 1 cup red lentils in 2.5 cups water until completely soft and absorbed, about 20 minutes. Cool slightly.

In a food processor, combine the lentils with 3 tbsp tahini, juice of 2 lemons, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp smoked paprika, salt, and ¼ cup olive oil. Process until silky. Add a tablespoon of cold water if too thick.

Transfer to a bowl, drizzle with more olive oil, dust with paprika and cumin, scatter with parsley. Serve with crudités or pita.
Red lentils. Genius. Plenty of those in my pantry.
